verbatim: normalization data transformation protocol: Low count mRNAs were filtered out prior to differential gene expression analysis. Only mRNAs with normalized read count (counts per million mapped reads, CPM) > 2 in at least 10 samples were retained for downstream analysis. ERCC spike-ins were used to evaluate library quality and estimate detection range. Remove Unwanted Variation from RNA-Seq Data (RUV-seq, v1.18.0) was used with RUVg() with empirically detected negative genes and ERCC spike ins to normalize and remove unwanted variations (Risso et al. 2014). Empirical negative control genes were identified with an ANOVA-like test comparing all conditions (FDR < 0.1). | high throughput sequence alignment protocol: A customized trimming script was used to trim off polyA sequences embedded in the adapter sequences. Only reads longer than 36bp after trimming were used. In addition, the first 12 nucleotides were trimmed based on manufacturer’s recommendations. Ribosomal reads which were over-represented in the samples through priming by oligo(dT) binding to A-rich regions in the ribosomal RNA loci were removed. Trimmed and filtered reads were aligned to the mouse genome (mm10) using a splice aware aligner, STAR (version 2.5.1b) with default settings except “--outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.05” for QuantSeq. QC of mapped RNA seq reads was performed using Qualimap (version 2.2.1).

The pooled samples were run thrice. Fastq and BAM files were merged using Picard Tools (v2.7.1). Alignment of fastq files to the mouse reference genome was conducted with STAR (v2.5.1b) using gene models from Ensembl v67 genome annotation. | Data was normalized using Pipeline Of RNA-Seq Transformations (PORT - v0.8.1-beta). Briefly, PORT recognizes potential confounding factors (e.g., ribosomal RNA and mitochondrial DNA) and omits these reads from the normalization process. Importantly, our samples had normal ranges and distributions of both ribosomal RNA (2.28 – 6.05%) and mitochondrial DNA (0.5 – 1.8%). Next, PORT identifies the input sample with the fewest number of gene-mapping reads and randomly re-samples each of the other datasets down to this minimum read count. This re-sampling approach accounts for batch effects and differences in sequencing depth between the samples, and allows for direct comparison between samples. | Genome_build: mm9 | Supplementary_files_format_and_content: txt file contains PORT-normalized and quantified read counts for each gene in each sample

Read alignment: Cell Ranger version 1.2 (10X Genomics, USA) was used to de-multiplex and quantify unique molecular identifiers (UMI). A count matrix was generated for each sample with default parameters and genes were mapped to the 10x reference for GRCm38 (mm10; for the scRNA-seq data set) or an adapted reference from 10x mm10-premrna to include introns (for the snRNA-seq data set), following the steps outlined on the 10x Genomics website (https://support.10xgenomics.com/single-cell-gene-expression/software/pipelines/latest/advanced/references). | Barcode filtering: Barcodes were filtered to include those with a total UMI count >10% of the 99th percentile of the expected recovered cells. | Quality control: The Scrublet tool was run with default parameters to identify likely doublets (this step was omitted for the snRNA-seq data) which were subsequently removed from the expression matrix. Further processing was performed using the Seurat50 R package (version 2.3). Cells in which <500 or >4,000 (>5,500 for the snRNA-seq data) expressed genes were detected, as well any cell with >20% (>5% for snRNA-seq) mitochondrial and/or ribosomal transcripts were discarded. Genes detected in <10 cells (<3 cells in the snRNA-seq data) were also removed. | Normalization: Counts were normalized using Seurat SCTransform | Genome_build: Mus Musculus reference genome build Grch38 – release 77 | Supplementary_files_format_and_content: nuclei_normdata.csv.gz: comma-separated, gzip archived. …

The sequencing libraries were multiplexed and clustered onto a flowcell. All data was analysed in Genespring GX12 (Agilent); .CEL files from the SL and the EU arrays (n=5) were uploaded subject to quartile RMA normalization where the median was used for baseline before statistical differences between the two conditions were determined using an unpaired t-test for unequal variance (Welch) with a Benjamini Hotchberg multiple test correction applied to maintain a corrected p-value of <0.05.
